metas.name: The Death of Yugoslavia
metas.description: Start here. Norma Percy's masterpiece, from the team behind Putin, Russia and the West: Milošević, Tuđman, Izetbegović and the rest explain, on camera, how they took Yugoslavia apart. Six parts.

metas.name: Putin vs the West
metas.description: Norma Percy's sequel to Putin, Russia and the West, picking up from 2014 through the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with the leaders who sat across from Putin. Three parts.

metas.name: Clash of the Superpowers: America vs China
metas.description: Norma Percy again, new this year: a decade of US-China rivalry from Trump's first term to now, with Bolton, McMaster, Jake Sullivan, Pelosi, Boris Johnson and Chinese officials. Two parts.

metas.name: Trump Takes on the World
metas.description: Norma Percy on Trump's first-term foreign policy, told by his own officials and the foreign leaders who dealt with him. Three parts.

metas.name: Castro's Revolution vs. The World
metas.description: Norma Percy on Cuba (UK title: Cuba: Castro vs the World): the missile crisis, Angola and the Soviet collapse, with Cuban, American and Russian insiders. Three parts.

metas.name: Inside Europe: 10 Years of Turmoil
metas.description: Norma Percy inside the EU's summit rooms: the euro crisis, Greece, the refugee crisis and Brexit, told by the prime ministers and presidents who argued it out. Three parts.

metas.name: Inside Obama's White House
metas.description: Norma Percy with Obama himself and his inner circle on how the big decisions were actually made. Four parts.

metas.name: Turning Point: The Bomb and the Cold War
metas.description: Same strand as the 9/11 Turning Point, but the full nuclear age from Hiroshima to Ukraine. Nine episodes, more strategy than battlefields.

metas.name: Cold War
metas.description: The generational one: CNN's 24-part history from 1945 to 1991, narrated by Kenneth Branagh, built on interviews with key players on both sides. Long, but each episode stands alone.

metas.name: Commanding Heights: The Battle for the World Economy
metas.description: PBS three-parter on the century-long fight between state and market, from Keynes and Hayek to globalisation, with the politicians and economists who made the calls.

metas.name: The Second Russian Revolution
metas.description: The Gorbachev years told from inside the Politburo, made just as the Soviet Union was falling apart. Pairs well with Meeting Gorbachev.

metas.name: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
metas.description: Dror Moreh's eight-part series: Kissinger, Powell, Albright, Wolfowitz and others on Iraq, Bosnia, Rwanda, Darfur and Syria, and when America should step in. The 2022 film cut is in the movies row.

metas.name: Turning Point: 9/11 and the War on Terror
metas.description: Five parts covering the whole arc, from the roots of al-Qaeda through Afghanistan and Iraq to the 2021 withdrawal. English.

metas.name: Human, All Too Human
metas.description: BBC, three hour-long episodes: Nietzsche, Heidegger, Sartre. Clear background for both Land and Derrida. Start with the Nietzsche episode.

metas.name: Frontline
metas.description: Watch these episodes: 'Money, Power and Wall Street' (2012, four parts, the most thorough account), 'The Warning' (2009, the failed fight to regulate derivatives) and 'The Untouchables' (2013, why no bankers were prosecuted). For US foreign policy: 'Ghosts of Rwanda' (2004, why the US and UN stood by during the genocide).

metas.name: Meltdown: The Secret History of the Global Collapse
metas.description: CBC, four parts. Global angle: Iceland, Europe and how the contagion spread.

metas.name: All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace
metas.description: Adam Curtis. Episode one covers Greenspan, Ayn Rand and the belief that markets stabilize themselves.
